meta.role: Junior Software Engineer, Field Service Platform

sources.title: One pipeline for every FieldLink team
Junior Software Engineer, Field Service Platform

company_claims.text: Orvanta Group manufactures commercial heating and cooling equipment and employs about 12,000 people in 31 countries.
In 2025 the group started a programme to move all field-service operations onto a single digital platform, run by Orvanta Digital, by 2028.

Orvanta Digital is the group's software unit, with teams in Columbus, Ohio, and Lyon, France; its Field Service Platform team builds FieldLink, the app service technicians use to receive work orders and log repairs.
Since June 2026 all FieldLink teams ship through one shared CI pipeline: every pull request needs an approved code review, passing automated tests and a security scan before release.
The role builds and tests backend features for FieldLink work orders, writes SQL against PostgreSQL, contributes to the shared CI pipeline and documents changes for the teams in Columbus and Lyon.
The Field Service Platform team may be hiring to add FieldLink capacity as more of the group's field-service operations move onto the platform before 2028.

letter.subject: Application: Junior Software Engineer, Field Service Platform

paragraphs.text: I am applying for the Junior Software Engineer role on the Field Service Platform team at Orvanta Digital, the software unit of Orvanta Group. The group plans to move all field-service operations by 2028 onto a single digital platform run by Orvanta Digital, and the team builds FieldLink, the app technicians use to receive work orders and log repairs.

In a capstone team of three, I owned the FastAPI backend and the route-batching heuristic for RouteWise. I designed its PostgreSQL schema for stops, drivers and routes, wrote pytest tests for the endpoints, and four volunteer coordinators used it in a three-week pilot. It is the same kind of tested backend work the posting describes for FieldLink work orders.

Your engineering blog describes one shared CI pipeline for all FieldLink teams, where every pull request needs passing automated tests and a security scan before release. AltCheck is the closest project I have to that pipeline: a GitHub Action that flags images without alt text in HTML pull requests, adopted by three student club websites.
My CV and project notes do not mention a formal code review process or Azure. My nearest practice is AltCheck, which runs on pull requests.

Documenting changes for the Columbus and Lyon teams is part of the role, and I am a native French speaker with fluent English, so I can write those notes in either language. If the team is adding FieldLink capacity as more field-service operations move onto the platform, I would welcome a conversation about where you need help first.

interview.question: How did you test the RouteWise endpoints?
interview.talking_points: pytest tests for the API endpoints; schema for stops, drivers and routes; limits: a 3-week pilot with 4 coordinators and survey-based time figures.

interview.question: What would you do in your first weeks under a formal approval process?
interview.talking_points: No formal approval process so far; AltCheck is the nearest practice; read the team's standards and ask for feedback on small changes first.

questions.ask: Was your code reviewed by others through pull requests (capstone team, club websites)? Links would let the application cite it.
questions.why: R4 (code review) is a required gap; reviewed pull requests would be partial evidence.

questions.why: Your documents state January 2027; the posting gives no start date.
